title: SRE bridge scrub + latency profiling — week of Jun 4 2028
content:
Summary:
This note captures the bridge-room scrub for this week, a short latency profiling exercise we ran against the text-generation route, and the on-call handoff checklist for the next rotation. The goal was to triage recurring 95th percentile spikes and make tactical runbook edits to reduce cognitive load during incidents.

What happened (high level):
- Friday 2028-06-02 03:40 UTC: brief degradation on /v1/generate for region eu-west-1. Clients observed p95 token latency spike to ~420ms (SLO target 200ms). No data loss; requests eventually served.
- Cause (post-bridge provisional): kube node eviction pressure on a small fleet of dedicated-serving instances (gpu-pool-a). Memory pressure triggered GC storms in the runtime and a fallback routing surge into older model variant (quantized) which had higher cold-start latency.
- Impact: ~3.7% of requests in eu-west-1 during the 12 minute window had p95 > 300ms. Affected service: hosted inference generation routes only. No effect on embeddings or private deployments.

Incident timeline (abbreviated):
- 03:40 UTC: on-call paged (pager SRE-4123). Initial alert: route p95 > 300ms for 5m.
- 03:43 UTC: bridge opened; on-call + Marcus (infra), Elena (runtime) joined.
- 03:50 UTC: identified node pressure metric pattern; autoscaler had not triggered due to burst duration.
- 03:54 UTC: manual scale-up of gpu-pool-a nodes by infra; routing throttled to avoid overloading fallback variants.
- 03:58 UTC: p95 back to ~190ms; bridge stood down at 04:05 UTC for monitoring.

Root cause analysis (working):
- Primary: kubelet memory eviction on 4/24 nodes in gpu-pool-a due to a combination of increased KV-cache retention (recent optimizer change) and a background model-compile job that was scheduled on those nodes.
- Secondary: autoscaler thresholds are tuned for sustained load, not short microbursts caused by prefix cache misses — leads to reactive manual scaling.
- Tertiary: fallback variant selection logic prioritizes model-compatibility but does not consider cold-start penalty.

SLO snapshot (as of 2028-06-04 00:00 UTC):
- generation.p95 (hosted, global): 210ms (7-day rolling average), target 200ms.
- embeddings.p99: 50ms, target 60ms.
- error_rate (hosted generation): 0.12%, target <0.25%.
- Ops note: generation.p95 shows a creeping tail—the median is still 60–80ms, but p95 drift is visible during regional microbursts.

Actions taken (this week):
1) Emergency: scaled gpu-pool-a + cordoned compile jobs off serving nodes (Marcus).
2) Mitigation: temporary routing policy change to prefer warm quantized variants only when their warm-start metric < 150ms (Elena).
3) Observability: added a derived metric for "fallback_cold_start_count" and a dashboard tile (Confluence link in linked_artifacts).
4) Runbook edits: clarified the escalation path when p95 > 300ms for > 3m; added checklist to prevent manual scaling errors (Samir).

Planned follow-ups (owner, due):
- SRE-4178 (Marcus) — autoscaler tuning spike-detection rule: introduce short-window (1m) derivative checks to trigger burst scale-up. Due: 2028-06-11.
- Runtime PR (Elena) — add latency-weighted scoring to fallback selection so cold-start cost is considered. PR opened: infra/pull/834. Due: 2028-06-15.
- Runbook refresh (Samir) — create a "microburst play" that runs through metrics to avoid knee-jerk manual scale decisions. Due: 2028-06-08.
- Postmortem doc (Aisha) — full RCA writeup once quant data is in. Target publish: 2028-06-12.

On-call handoff (next rotation):
- New on-call: Derek Huang (primary), backup: Priya Nair.
- Key watch items for this rotation:
   * gpu-pool-a memory pressure trendline (alerts: gpu-pool-a.mem.evictions > 1/m)
   * fallback_cold_start_count spike (> 10/min)
   * generation.p95 regional deviation (> +80ms over baseline)
- Slack escalation path: @oncall -> #sre-ops -> pager escalation.
- Handoff checklist: confirm cordon status of compile nodes; verify autoscaler derivative rule is deployed to staging; ensure warm-variant latency test ran in the last 6h.

Runbook / tooling notes:
- We added a small scripting helper (scripts/check-warm-variants.sh) to run a 30s probe and report median token latency. Encourage on-call to run before doing manual routing changes.
- Observability gap: we need a per-variant rolling warm-start histogram (1m windows). Filed as SRE-4189 (linked in git and JIRA).

Risks and open questions:
- If autoscaler tuning is too aggressive it could overspend for short-lived microbursts — need to model cost impact (finance input requested, tagged finance/ops).
- How long until runtime patch lands that changes fallback scoring? If delayed, consider a temporary circuit-breaker limiting fallback traffic.
- Is model-compile scheduling on serving nodes acceptable? We should consider a dedicated compile pool or stronger pod affinity rules.

Notes to self / messy thoughts (intended for reviewers):
- We saw two other small spikes earlier in the week that looked similar; saved the flamegraphs to /mnt/sre/latency-profiles/2028-06-01. Might be same underlying pattern.
- P95 drift might be exacerbated by an optimizer change rolled last month — correlate PR deploy dates vs tail increases.
- Consider short-lived reserve capacity for high-risk regions during major model rollouts. Could be a feature for Dedicated customers too.

Meeting asks / blockers for next sync:
- Infra: provide cost estimate for 1m derivative autoscale vs baseline. (Marcus)
- Runtime: status on PR infra/pull/834 and estimated time to merge. (Elena)
- Observability: ETA on variant warm-start histogram; plan for alerts. (Samir)

Appendix (useful links and quick references):
- Incident tracker: JIRA SRE-4123
- Autoscaler tuning ticket: JIRA SRE-4178
- Runtime fallback PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/834
- Slack archive: #sre-ops thread 2028-06-02 "eu-west-1 p95 spike"

If anything is missing or you want me to drop a short runbook diff into Confluence for sign-off before next rotation, ping me.

-- Aisha
